title: Praise melts what comparison hardens
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
summary: The shabad opens with metal merging into metal and uses that image to describe praise absorbed into the Praiseworthy Lord. It carries the listener through saintly dust, true action, and the home of the self being found within.
whyItMatters: This is for anyone whose mind keeps hardening around comparison, self-consciousness, or restless ambition. Kept near, it softens the separate self and turns it toward praise, holy company, and homecoming.
takeaway: Let praise, saintly company, and true action soften the self into homecoming.

lines.gurmukhi: ਧਾਤੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਫੁਨਿ ਧਾਤੁ ਕਉ ਸਿਫਤੀ ਸਿਫਤਿ ਸਮਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhaat milai fun dhaat kau sifatee sifat samai ||
lines.translation: As metal merges with metal, those who chant the Praises of the Lord are absorbed into the Praiseworthy Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਲਾਲੁ ਗੁਲਾਲੁ ਗਹਬਰਾ ਸਚਾ ਰੰਗੁ ਚੜਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: laal gulaal gahabaraa sachaa ra(n)g chaRaau ||
lines.translation: Like the poppies, they are dyed in the deep crimson color of Truthfulness.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਏਕੈ ਭਾਇ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: sach milai sa(n)tokheeaa har jap ekai bhai ||1||
lines.translation: Those contented souls who meditate on the Lord with single-minded love, meet the True Lord. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਾਈ ਰੇ ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhaiee re sa(n)t janaa kee ren ||
lines.translation: O Siblings of Destiny, become the dust of the feet of the humble Saints.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤ ਸਭਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਈਐ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਪਦਾਰਥੁ ਧੇਣੁ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)t sabhaa gur paieeaai mukat padhaarath dhen ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: In the Society of the Saints, the Guru is found. He is the Treasure of Liberation, the Source of all good fortune. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਊਚਉ ਥਾਨੁ ਸੁਹਾਵਣਾ ਊਪਰਿ ਮਹਲੁ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: uoochau thaan suhaavanaa uoopar mahal muraar ||
lines.translation: Upon that Highest Plane of Sublime Beauty, stands the Mansion of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਚੁ ਕਰਣੀ ਦੇ ਪਾਈਐ ਦਰੁ ਘਰੁ ਮਹਲੁ ਪਿਆਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: sach karanee dhe paieeaai dhar ghar mahal piaar ||
lines.translation: By true actions, this human body is obtained, and the door within ourselves which leads to the Mansion of the Beloved, is found.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਨੁ ਸਮਝਾਈਐ ਆਤਮ ਰਾਮੁ ਬੀਚਾਰਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh man samajhaieeaai aatam raam beechaar ||2||
lines.translation: The Gurmukhs train their minds to contemplate the Lord, the Supreme Soul. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਤ੍ਰਿਬਿਧਿ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਈਅਹਿ ਆਸ ਅੰਦੇਸਾ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: tirabidh karam kamaie'eeh aas a(n)dhesaa hoi ||
lines.translation: By actions committed under the influence of the three qualities, hope and anxiety are produced.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਉ ਗੁਰ ਬਿਨੁ ਤ੍ਰਿਕੁਟੀ ਛੁਟਸੀ ਸਹਜਿ ਮਿਲਿਐ ਸੁਖੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: kiau gur bin tirakuTee chhuTasee sahaj miliaai sukh hoi ||
lines.translation: Without the Guru, how can anyone be released from these three qualities? Through intuitive wisdom, we meet with Him and find peace.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਮਹਲੁ ਪਛਾਣੀਐ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇ ਮਲੁ ਧੋਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: nij ghar mahal pachhaaneeaai nadhar kare mal dhoi ||3||
lines.translation: Within the home of the self, the Mansion of His Presence is realized when He bestows His Glance of Grace and washes away our pollution. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਬਿਨੁ ਗੁਰ ਮੈਲੁ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਕਿਉ ਘਰ ਵਾਸੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bin gur mail na utarai bin har kiau ghar vaas ||
lines.translation: Without the Guru, this pollution is not removed. Without the Lord, how can there be any homecoming?

lines.gurmukhi: ਏਕੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਵੀਚਾਰੀਐ ਅਵਰ ਤਿਆਗੈ ਆਸ ॥
lines.transliteration: eko sabadh veechaareeaai avar tiaagai aas ||
lines.translation: Contemplate the One Word of the Shabad, and abandon other hopes.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਖਿ ਦਿਖਾਈਐ ਹਉ ਸਦ ਬਲਿਹਾਰੈ ਜਾਸੁ ॥੪॥੧੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak dhekh dhikhaieeaai hau sadh balihaarai jaas ||4||12||
lines.translation: O Nanak, I am forever a sacrifice to the one who beholds, and inspires others to behold Him. ||4||12||

structure: The shabad begins by picturing praise as fusion instead of performance.
From there it turns toward saintly company, true action, and the Guru as the way beyond anxiety and the three qualities.
The closing movement rests in homecoming, where other hopes are abandoned and the One is beheld.
